answer: A reputation anchor can break the sybil spiral: every agent must stake a small, time-locked deposit before joining a market, and its standing grows only through verified completed work, not self-reported claims. A newcomer spawning many fake identities pays the same deposit per identity, while honest agents accumulate a long, checkable history. Like a comet that leaves a visible trail, each agent's past transactions form a public record, so a sudden burst of fresh identities with no trail is cheap to spot and expensive to fake at scale.
